catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds the native get_image parameter set. cap.imaging.capture.v1 is keyed by exposure, binning, camera and ROI, while the clone passes resolution (width and height), pixel_size and dwell_time and returns the frame data; cap.sensing.image.v1 has the same mismatch. The extension carries those fields, plus the native invert flag, and returns a reference to the written 16-bit PGM.

cap.imaging.focus.v1 requires a method input and returns z_um and focused, but the upstream auto_focus takes only a baseline flag, returns None and exposes no working-distance getter (smartem/online/microscope.py:244-275). The extension records only that the native call returned; claiming a z position or a focus score would invent a fact.

No catalogue class binds an input-less one-shot instrument preparation sequence. cap.device.configure.v1 is a writable-state patch and cannot express an action; the upstream prepare_acquisition is a fixed sequence of contrast, focus, lens-alignment and stig calls (smartem/online/microscope.py:236-242).

cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is a robot-arm class (resource kinds robot.arm) in millimetres with an orientation, and cap.motion.joint_position.v1 is a joint array in radians. The upstream move takes five raw stage coordinates (x, y, z, r, t) whose unit the clone does not state (smartem/online/microscope.py:387-399), so the extension declares unit 1 and operator-required bounds instead of pretending to convert.

No catalogue class binds the upstream shutdown. cap.motion.stop.v1 is for motion, and cap.device.configure.v1 is a writable-state patch. The upstream class has no stop or blank method; its only shutdown is close() (smartem/online/microscope.py:226-228), which this safe_state action calls and which is also the @estop.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PythonObjectDriver (family python-object) and decision direct-driver. The package is a direct Driver over the card's entry symbol, smartem.online.microscope:ThermoFisherVerios, because the family command table can call native methods but cannot write and size-check the returned frame as an artifact, cannot validate the frame shape, and cannot express the five-coordinate stage move plus the native close safe state. The entry symbol was confirmed in the clone at smartem/online/microscope.py:167.

MOCK PATH: the card prefers upstream-sim, but the upstream FakeRandomMicroscope (smartem/online/microscope.py:43) is a BaseMicroscope fake for the SmartEM orchestrator, not the ThermoFisherVerios interface: it has no auto_focus or prepare_acquisition and its get_image has a different parameter contract. The package fake is a stateful in-memory stand-in for ThermoFisherVerios with the same public method names and synchronous shape; it never imports or runs the upstream package or the proprietary autoscript SDK. The fake's image size cap and pixel values are test data marked as placeholders in fake.py, not facts.

NOT COVERED: the pixel array is not carried in the receipt. x-cap.cfpark00.acquire_image.v1 returns image_ref, the path of a 16-bit PGM written in the system temporary directory, plus width and height. The fake returns at most a 16 x 16 placeholder frame, while the real get_image returns the requested resolution; the clone's example parameters use 2048 x 1768 (examples/default_smartem_params.json:2-10), which is an example configuration, not a fixed device bound. Also not covered: the scan-rotation theta input, the rescan_map and patterning path, detector selection, and auto_contrast_brightness and auto_stig as separate actions; prepare_acquisition invokes the upstream preparation sequence that includes them. No reads are exposed because the class has no read or query method: the resource state is empty and a front-panel change is not visible.

UNITS AND LIMITS: dwell_time is in seconds because the clone multiplies the dwell time by 1e9 and labels the result ns (smartem/smartem.py:280). Width and height are pixels (unit 1). The clone does not state the unit of pixel_size or of the five stage coordinates, so they are declared with unit 1 and every numeric action input is Limit.operator_required; all calls are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies its envelope. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay only, not a device fact; fixtures/conformance.json holds test inputs only. No numeric Limit was copied from a class or constructor default.

SAFETY: the declared risk is R3 because this is a scanning electron microscope (README.md:21) with an electron column and a moving specimen stage. The upstream class unblanks the electron beam in initialize (smartem/online/microscope.py:224) and exposes no blank, halt or stop method. The @estop and the safe_state=True action x-cap.cfpark00.release_microscope.v1 therefore call the native close(), which disconnects the vendor client and deletes the client handle (smartem/online/microscope.py:226-228). No independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the safe-state action satisfies SAFE-045. The driver guards close() with an instance flag because the e-stop runs the @estop and then the safe-state action. The upstream close has no timeout parameter, so a blocking vendor disconnect is a residual hardware risk. The loader refuses the hardware backend of this model-authored R3 package until a human signs reviewed_by; that protection applies at R2 and R3 only, and it is not claimed for lower-risk packages.

LICENCE: the card records MIT, a permissive licence, and the clone is unmodified (git status clean); the gate G1 passed. check-report.json is generated by the gate and is not hand-edited.
